quotes.quote: OmniVideoBench comprises 1000 high-quality question-answer(QA) pairs, each annotated with step-by-step reasoning traces, derived from 628 diverse videos ranging from several seconds to 30 minutes, and manually verified to guarantee complete correctness and uniqueness.
OmniVideoBench encompasses 13 carefully designed question types, covering temporal reasoning, spatial localization, counting, causal inference, summarization, and beyond

Current MLLMs have not achieved a passing score (<60%) on OmniVideoBench. The best-performing model, Gemini-2.0-Pro, only achieves an accuracy of 58.90%. Except for the newly proposed Qwen3-Omni, the performance of open-source models is close to random.
Gemini-2.5-Pro only achieves 38.46% accuracy on videos with music signal, while the results on sound and speech are 57.72% and 61.66%, respectively.
the accuracy results on the relationship reasoning and summarization tasks are more than 80%
OmniVideoBench is composed of real-world videos sourced from YouTube
we categorize videos into eight broad classes: Vlog, News, Cartoon, Sports, Documentary, TV, Ego, and Others
we first designed multiple-choice questions consisting of the question stem, the correct answer, and several distractors

we obtained approximately 2,500 QA pairs. We categorize the tasks into 13 types: Fine-grained Perception, Spatial Reasoning, Attribute Comparison, Background & Music Understanding, Counting, Temporal Understanding, Summarization, Sentiment Analysis, Causal Reasoning, Relationship Reasoning, Reference Reasoning, Ego Reasoning, and Hypothetical Reasoning

We employed an advanced MLLM (i.e., Gemini 2.0 Flash), with strong audiovisual perception and comprehension capabilities, as well as long-context processing ability, to filter out questions that could be resolved using only a single modality.
After this filtering stage, approximately 1,500 questions were retained.
we employed a large language model, DeepSeek-V3.1 (Liu et al., 2024a), with strong reasoning capabilities to filter out questions that could be answered solely based on textual information
After this stage of refinement, 1103 questions were retained.
Through this process, we obtained 1000 high-quality QA pairs with explicit step-by-step reasoning chains
our OmniVideoBench dataset consists of 628 real-world videos with audio tracks, spanning 8 major categories and 68 subcategories
with an average duration of 384.6 seconds, an average resolution of 480p, about 2k ASR … transcribed tokens per video, and roughly three speakers per video
The reasoning process covers both modalities, with 54% of steps grounded in vision and 46% in audio. There are 762, 147, 91 QA pairs related to Speech, Sound and Music, respectively

we restrict our selection to videos published after June 2024. We use the most recent videos possible to mitigate unfairness and potential overestimation issues arising from the model having already been exposed to similar content during training.
We excluded videos with embedded subtitles, as such practices convey most of the audio information visually, enabling models to “cheat” through vision alone.
To ensure video quality, we require a minimum resolution of 480p
